customer: Hi, so I'm a college student here in Virginia and I'm thinking about selling my midsize SUV to help cover tuition, but there's kind of a weird situation with it. The odometer stopped working a while back and my uncle's mechanic swapped in a different one, so now the number on the dash is way lower than what the car has actually driven, I think. I'm not sure if that's a huge problem or if I just need to explain it somewhere, and honestly I don't want to accidentally do something wrong when I sell it.
agent: Thanks for reaching out, and good call checking first. Per our article "Broken or replaced odometer," please let us know the odometer was replaced when you request your offer, and at the appointment you'll mark 'not actual mileage' on the odometer statement, form NW-ODO-1. Vehicles marked 'not actual mileage' receive a reduced offer, but if you know the true mileage, bring records that show it, such as service invoices.
